requirements.text: The system must provide an electronic method to create, amend and delete ISINs for electronically issued money market instruments.
The system must use SWIFT (ISO15022 standards) as the communication protocol.
The system must use MT 598 User Defined SWIFT messages as the format for messages.
The system must provide ISINs automatically in response to an electronic request (SWIFT).
The system must use an ISIN prefix of ZAM for money market instruments.
The system must use the branch code “ISN” as an extension of the JSE’s current BIC address (XJSEZAJJXISN).
The system must provide a screen for Clearing & Settlement to input manual ISINs on BCP.
The system must provide a screen to update issuer codes.
The system must provide a screen reflecting rejections from the JSE to STRATE for the previous day.
The system must provide a screen reflecting rejections from STRATE to the JSE for the previous day.
The system must send an email to Clearing & Settlement at the time of rejection.
The system must provide a screen to look up details per ISIN.
The system must implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to ensure that only authorized personnel can view, create, amend, or delete ISIN data and system configurations.
The system must maintain an immutable audit log of all user actions, including requests, rejections, manual updates, and system configuration changes, for a minimum of 7 years.
All data in transit must be encrypted using industry-standard protocols (e.g., TLS 1.2+), and sensitive data at rest must be encrypted using FIPS 140-2 compliant modules.
The system must process and respond to an ISIN issuance request within [X] seconds of receipt.
The system must support a peak throughput of [X] requests per minute and maintain availability during high-volume trading periods.
The system must achieve an RTO of [X] minutes and an RPO of [Y] minutes in the event of a site failure.
The system must maintain online access to the last 12 months of ISIN data and provide a mechanism for long-term archival beyond this period.
The system must process and respond to an ISIN issuance request within 5 seconds of receipt under a load of 500 requests per day.
The system must support a peak throughput of 50 requests per hour and maintain performance during concurrent access by multiple participants.
The system must return search results for ISIN queries within 2 seconds for datasets up to 12 months of history.
